blocks.text: The experiment investigates singular value decomposition (SVD), optimal low-rank approximation, image compression, and shared-basis representations. All five image tasks in the course handout are implemented: grayscale reconstruction, the RGB rank grid, metrics for every rank, three diagnostic curves, and an evidence-based discussion of the three key findings. The extension covers Eigenfaces, coefficient quantization, a synthetic three-dimensional surface, and synthetic temporal coefficients.

The RGB input is the 512 x 512 astronaut image distributed with scikit-image v0.25.2 (NASA image credit). Pixel values are converted to float64 and divided by 255. Eigenfaces uses the archived AT&T/ORL database: 400 real grayscale photographs, 40 subjects, and 112 x 92 pixels per image [2, 3]. The original inputs are included with the experiment.
1.1 Assembly and consistency of the supplied matrices

The numerical matrix printed in the handout agrees with A = Q5 Sigma Q4, where Q4 acts as V-transpose. The maximum elementwise difference is 3.276e-05; replacing Q4 by its transpose gives a difference of 41.700658. The first discrepancy is consistent with six-decimal input rounding. The main experiment uses the assembled matrix; the printed matrix is retained separately for comparison. Exact input arrays appear in the saved NPZ and Appendix A.
Assembled A (5 x 4)

The handout calls Q5 and Q4 positive definite, but these nonsymmetric matrices are approximately orthogonal: their Frobenius orthogonality residuals are 2.284e-06 and 2.176e-06. No reorthogonalization is applied to the given rounded entries.
1.2 Mathematical representation

blocks.word: A = UΣVᵀ = Σᵢ σᵢuᵢvᵢᵀ;   Aₖ = Σᵢ₌₁ᵏ σᵢuᵢvᵢᵀ
blocks.latex: A=U\Sigma V^T=\sum_{i=1}^{r}\sigma_i u_i v_i^T,\qquad A_k=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\sigma_i u_i v_i^T.

blocks.text: For a real m x n matrix, reduced SVD returns U of size m x r, V-transpose of size r x n and descending singular values, with r = min(m,n). Retaining the leading k terms gives a best rank-at-most-k approximation in the Frobenius norm. Reduced output is distinct from truncation: full_matrices=False controls returned shapes; slicing selects k [4].

title: 2. Matrix singular values, rank and energy

blocks.text: A teaching implementation obtains the eigenpairs of A-transpose A using numpy.linalg.eigh, orders them by descending eigenvalue, takes square roots to obtain singular values, and forms each left vector as A v / sigma. It is cross-checked against numpy.linalg.svd. Forming A-transpose A squares the condition number, so direct SVD is used for the image and face experiments.

blocks.word: Avᵢ = σᵢuᵢ;  Aᵀuᵢ = σᵢvᵢ;  AᵀAvᵢ = σᵢ²vᵢ;  AAᵀuᵢ = σᵢ²uᵢ
blocks.latex: Av_i=\sigma_i u_i,\quad A^Tu_i=\sigma_i v_i,\quad A^TAv_i=\sigma_i^2v_i,\quad AA^Tu_i=\sigma_i^2u_i.

blocks.text: Because A is rectangular, u and v are singular vectors of A. They are eigenvectors of A A-transpose and A-transpose A, respectively; they are not ordinary eigenvectors of the rectangular matrix itself.

All four singular values are nonzero, so A has rank 4 and full column rank. Its two-norm condition number is 100000.071. The first two components retain about 99.999901% of the energy, but this does not change the exact rank. A-transpose A has four positive eigenvalues, approximately 10000, 100, 0.01 and 0.000001. A A-transpose has one additional zero eigenvalue.

The two implementations differ in singular values by at most 5.487e-11. Summing all four rank-one terms gives a reconstruction residual of 5.975e-14. The measured relative reconstruction error at k=4 is a floating-point residual; the mathematical truncated-SVD tail is exactly zero.
Left and right singular vectors
Reduced U: each column is a left singular vector
V-transpose: each row transposes to a right singular vector
A paired sign change in a left and right vector leaves its rank-one term unchanged. Tables are rounded for readability; full precision is retained in matrix_decomposition.npz.

blocks.word: Rᵢ = σᵢuᵢvᵢᵀ;  A = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + R₄

blocks.text: The four components below are the requested explicit rank-one decomposition. Each component is 5 x 4, and A_k is obtained by adding the first k components. The full-precision arrays are also saved individually as CSV files.

The first component carries almost all of the large-scale magnitude. Later terms are much smaller, yet the fourth term is essential for exact rank 4. A visually negligible or numerically small component is not identical to a zero component.
4.1 Three-line core implementation (Task 1)

A = img @ np.array([0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722])
U, s, Vt = np.linalg.svd(A, full_matrices=False)
A_k = (U[:, :20] * s[:20]) @ Vt[:20, :]

The input img is an RGB floating-point array in [0,1]. The weighted sum produces a grayscale matrix. For k=20, the actual reconstruction shape is (512,512). The reconstruction is clipped to [0,1] for display only; raw error identities use the unclipped matrix.

blocks.caption: Figure 1. Original grayscale image and its rank-20 reconstruction.

blocks.text: 4.2 Metrics without explicit reconstruction (Task 3)

Let T be the sum of squared singular values over all three color channels, and let R(k) be the sum of squared singular values discarded after rank k. Orthogonal invariance of the Frobenius norm gives the following formulas, with pixel peak value 1:

blocks.word: T = ΣcΣᵢ σc,ᵢ²;  R(k) = ΣcΣᵢ>ₖ σc,ᵢ²;  E(k) = 1−R(k)/T
Relative error = √(R(k)/T);  MSE = R(k)/(HWC);  PSNR = 10 log₁₀(1/MSE)

blocks.text: For each channel, U needs Hk scalars, singular values need k, and V-transpose needs kW. The +1 term accounts for the singular values. Reverse cumulative sums compute the tails and avoid cancellation from subtracting nearly equal total and prefix energies. At full rank the theoretical MSE is zero and PSNR is infinity.

title: 5. RGB rank grid and numerical results

blocks.text: Each RGB channel is decomposed separately, truncated at the same k, and stacked to reconstruct a color image (Task 2). The prescribed ranks are 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 20, 35, 50, 80 and 120. The original plus these eleven reconstructions form the required 3 x 4 grid.

blocks.name: 02_rgb_rank_grid.png
blocks.caption: Figure 2. RGB reconstruction grid. Display values are clipped; titles use theoretical, unclipped PSNR.

blocks.text: All 512 rows, for k=1 through 512, are supplied in image_metrics_all_k.csv. Seven independent explicit reconstructions at k=1,4,20,80,120,256,512 confirm the singular-value tail identity against pixelwise error. Clipped MSE is recorded separately in image_error_validation.csv, because clipping changes the error measure.

blocks.name: 03_singular_values.png
blocks.caption: Figure 3. Singular values of R, G and B on a logarithmic vertical scale.

blocks.name: 04_error_psnr.png
blocks.caption: Figure 4. Relative error decreases and PSNR increases with k. The infinite full-rank PSNR is omitted from the finite curve.

blocks.name: 05_compression_ratio.png
blocks.caption: Figure 5. Parameter compression ratio and the rank at which the parameter count equals the pixel count.

blocks.text: The singular-value spectra decay rapidly, allowing small ranks to represent broad structures. Quality improves as k increases, while the parameter compression ratio falls. Once k exceeds the break-even rank, the factor representation contains more scalars than the original image.
7.1 Energy trap

At k=1, retained energy is 78.5057% but PSNR is only 11.856 dB. At k=4, energy reaches 90.5566% while PSNR is 15.428 dB. Even k=20 retains 97.9497% with PSNR 22.061 dB. Large color regions and global brightness dominate squared energy; high retained energy alone does not imply good visual fidelity.
7.2 Break-even point: scalars versus actual bytes

For the actual 512 x 512 image, k* = 255.750244. Therefore k<=255 reduces the scalar count and k>=256 increases it. The handout's approximately 353 belongs to a different 620 x 820 image and is not reused as a measured value.

This comparison assumes equal bytes per scalar. The RGB uint8 pixel payload is 786,432 B. Rank-20 float32 factors need 246,000 B, giving a byte ratio of 3.197, compared with the parameter ratio 12.788. The float32-versus-uint8 break-even rank is only 63.938; k>=64 expands the raw byte payload. The source PNG is 791,555 B and has its own encoding overhead. No comparison with JPEG was performed.
7.3 Detail loss

blocks.name: 06_detail_crop.png
blocks.caption: Figure 6. Identical image crop at the original resolution and at ranks 1, 4 and 20.

blocks.text: Suit seams, the badge and equipment boundaries become indistinct before broad orange regions disappear. This supports the observed loss of fine detail at low rank in this image. Small singular values are not universally equivalent to high spatial frequencies, so the observation is not asserted as a theorem for every image.
These answers are based on the generated figures and measured metrics. No classroom discussion attendance, group contribution or human observation session is fabricated.

Eigenfaces uses a shared PCA basis for both compression and recognition [5]. Each image is flattened to D=10304 entries. A training-only mean is subtracted before SVD of the centered training matrix. The leading rows of V-transpose are the shared basis B_k.

Nearest-neighbor classification compares Euclidean distances between coefficient vectors and returns the label of the closest training photograph. Per subject, a seeded permutation chooses seven training and three test photographs: 280 training and 120 test images overall. Seed 20260917 is retained for reproducibility. Training and test filenames never overlap. The mean, basis and quantization parameters are fitted only on training images.

The principal evaluation uses k=80, fixed before evaluating this run. Other ranks are sensitivity results, not a test-set search for a new optimum. This is closed-set recognition: the identities are present in training, but their test photographs are withheld. It does not measure recognition of previously unseen identities.

blocks.name: 08_mean_eigenfaces.png
blocks.caption: Figure 7. Training mean and the first eleven eigenfaces, each visualized on its own grayscale range.

blocks.text: The centered training matrix has numerical rank 279. The basis orthogonality residual is 6.772e-14. Eigenfaces are signed spatial patterns, not additional face photographs. The recorded split and all k=80 predictions are included as CSV files.

The primary result is 118/120 correct, or 98.33%. The descriptive sample-level Wilson 95% interval is [94.13%, 99.54%]. Photographs from a subject are related, and a single random split does not establish cross-identity or real-world generalization.

blocks.name: 09_face_reconstructions.png
blocks.caption: Figure 8. Three held-out test photographs and their shared-basis reconstructions.

blocks.text: The denominator includes the mean, basis and all N coefficient vectors. For N=280 and k=80 the scalar ratio is 3.366. The byte ratio additionally depends on dtype. At k=200 and 279, reconstruction PSNR improves while recognition accuracy falls to 96.67%; better reconstruction need not imply better classification. A held-out image may contain components outside the training subspace, so keeping every nonzero training component still does not reconstruct it exactly.

title: 10. Shared-basis upload and int8 coefficient quantization

blocks.text: This extension is a local encoder/decoder experiment on real ORL images, not an edge-device deployment. It uses k=32. For each dimension, the 0.1% and 99.9% training-coefficient quantiles define lo and hi. Quantization parameters are not fitted to test images.

rows: Maximum pixel change from float reconstruction
Nearest-neighbor accuracy after quantizing both sets
Shared model raw bytes / NPZ file
Ratio including shared model, first 120 frames
First frame count with total raw-byte savings

blocks.text: The model includes the float32 basis, mean, lo and scale. Its SHA-256 identifier and version are saved with the coefficients. Loading the saved model and decoding the actual int8 bytes is numerically cross-checked. Both endpoints must agree on the basis ID, version and normalization; unknown versions require model synchronization. ORL inputs already use fixed dimensions and division by 255, so no per-frame brightness standardization metadata is used here.

The 322-fold per-frame payload ratio excludes the shared model. Including the model needs at least 133 frames to save raw pixel bytes; packet headers, retransmission and security metadata are excluded. The small mean PSNR loss does not eliminate local distortion: the maximum pixel change is 0.021111, not the handout example of 0.0015.

Projection is not encryption or proven anonymization. These coefficients still allow identity recognition, and a party with the basis can approximately reconstruct faces. Discarding leading components as a privacy measure was not evaluated.

title: 11. Three-dimensional shared basis: a teaching simulation

blocks.text: The original 3D Morphable Model represents aligned three-dimensional shape and texture using separate learned means and PCA bases [6]. Its shape representation can be written as a mean shape plus a weighted sum of shape modes; texture uses an analogous model.

blocks.word: S = μS + Σᵢ αᵢbᵢ;  T = μT + Σᵢ βᵢcᵢ

blocks.text: No licensed real 3D face scans were supplied. To demonstrate the shared-basis mechanism, a synthetic surface uses a 40 x 32 grid (1280 vertices, 3840 coordinate entries) and six linear deformation modes. A fixed seed generates 200 surfaces, with 160 for training and 40 for testing. This is a controlled simulation, not a scanned human face or a fitted real 3DMM. Texture PCA and photo-to-3D fitting are not implemented.

blocks.name: 11_synthetic_3dmm.png
blocks.caption: Figure 9. Synthetic surface and low-rank reconstruction; no real human scan is shown.

blocks.text: At k=6 the reconstruction reaches floating-point precision because the data generator has exactly six linear deformation degrees of freedom. This validates the code under its construction assumptions; it does not imply that real three-dimensional faces need only six coefficients. A true 3DMM experiment additionally requires licensed scans, consistent vertex correspondence, and independent evaluation on real faces.

title: 12. Temporal shared basis: a teaching simulation

blocks.text: ORL is a static photograph database; filename order is not a measured time sequence. The temporal extension therefore explicitly generates 300 frames of 32-dimensional coefficient trajectories. A held-out face coefficient vector is perturbed by smooth sinusoids with amplitude 0.12 times each training coefficient standard deviation. The training-fitted quantizer is reused.

blocks.name: 10_synthetic_temporal_coefficients.png
blocks.caption: Figure 10. The first four synthetic coefficient trajectories; these are not measured video frames.

blocks.text: An absolute coefficient reset is inserted every 60 frames; other frames store differences from the preceding quantized frame. Differences are stored as int16 because they may exceed the int8 range. zlib level 9 is applied to both direct and differential representations for a fair comparison. Decoding recovers every quantized coefficient exactly, and compressed bytes pass a round-trip check.

Differential coding gives an additional factor of 1.427 relative to directly zlib-compressed coefficients: 1979 B versus 1387 B. This does not reproduce the handout's illustrative factor of 2 to 3. Without entropy compression, int16 differencing doubles the coefficient payload. Including one shared-model transfer, the 300-frame ratio relative to raw uint8 frames is 2.270.

Lossless recovery applies to the already quantized coefficients, not the original image pixels. The smoothness was deliberately built into the simulation. Absolute resets restore predictor state but do not retrain the PCA basis. Scene-change detection, pose-drift detection, basis updates and comparisons against JPEG or video codecs remain untested; those mechanisms are design proposals rather than measured production results.
13.1 Conclusions

The supplied matrix has rank 4 with singular values spanning five orders of magnitude. Two terms retain nearly all energy, while all four are required for exact reconstruction. The left/right eigenvector identities and the rank-one sum agree with numerical reference results.

For images, SVD produces a controlled fidelity-storage tradeoff. Energy, relative error, PSNR, scalar count and actual byte count describe different aspects and must be reported separately. The 512 x 512 image reaches a scalar break-even rank of 255.750, but float32 factors exceed the raw uint8 payload from k=64 onward.

A shared basis unifies face reconstruction and closed-set recognition. The measured k=80 result is 118/120, or 98.33%, for one reproducible split. A training-only quantizer permits small int8 coefficient payloads, but model transfer and local clipping errors must be included. Synthetic 3D and temporal experiments validate mechanisms under explicit construction assumptions.

What was measured

Matrix SVD, image metrics and reconstructions, ORL Eigenfaces classification, local int8 coefficient decoding, model byte counts, and the controlled synthetic 3D/temporal examples were executed. Values in this report are read from the current results JSON/CSV files. Figures are generated directly by the same run.
What was not established

The experiment does not establish real-device latency, actual network transfer, real 3D-face reconstruction accuracy, real-video coding gains, scene-change robustness, privacy protection, or generalization to unseen identities. The handout's citation counts and illustrative performance numbers are not reported as current measurements.
